title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall (SIBDH, C:autonomous-heredity): wall layer, divisions and death-driven selection against the inert marker all replicate on fresh seed 6; Supported
summary: Re-ran world.py on fresh seed 6 with labkit (rerun/seed6, 100k steps) and the author's genealogy.py on the same seed (data/gen_s6.json.gz), read with the author's deathsel.py and birthfate.py (data/selection_s6.txt). From a noisy start, 13-24 cells form; labkit gives the M wall layer at rim/core 2.94, rim/outside 4.9, 99/115 bodies individually membrane-like (claim: 3.0/2.96), and 7 persistent splits (max generation 2, merge/split 0.33); the genealogy gives 9 persistent splits to generation 2, 0 merges and 51 intrinsic whole-cell deaths. Selection replicates against the identical-event inert marker carried by the same particles: dying mature cells sit at the 4th yield percentile (22 deaths, all below the median) against the 54th for the marker; 10/12 low-born cells die against 4/12 high-born (marker 7/13 and 7/11); dying cells were already low at birth (rank 0.22, marker 0.50); population mean yield rises 1.00 -> 1.17 while the marker ends at 0.98.

verdicts.limitation: Lineages are shallow (generation 2 on seed 6, the minimum for from-noise D) and one large irregular body persists through the run; the M layer is passive (no feedback, as the claim states), so B is a self-made adsorbed layer, not a working membrane; the selected trait is continuous, so 'kinds' are yield ranks; I used the author's analysis scripts unchanged.
